newsitem.title: FRANCE: French unions to consult truckers on ending strike.
newsitem.headline: French unions to consult truckers on ending strike.

text.p: French truck drivers' unions reported substantial progress on the key issue of working time in talks on Friday and said they would consult truckers manning roadblocks around the country on an end to the 12-day strike.

"Important progress has been made in the negotiations. The draft decree on work time seems to move things forward significantly. We are going to put all these issues to the grassroots and ask workers to decide on the future of the strike," a spokesman for the militant Communist-led CGT said.
The biggest union, the Socialist-led CFDT, also spoke of "substantial progress" and said it was up to the drivers at the roadblocks to make up their minds.

"Our feeling is that our profession has won dignity and recognition in these 12 days of struggle," CFDT spokesman Claude Debons told reporters after the unions and employers signed five agreements on early retirement, sick pay, travel expenses, union rights and a ban on Sunday driving.

Employers doubled their offer of a special bonus payment to 3,000 francs ($600) in a bid to clinch an end to the strike that is strangling the French economy, and the government promised a decree within two weeks on the key issue of work time.

First indications from the grassroots were that drivers had begun to vote with their wheels by lifting some roadblocks, but 210 barrages were still in place at 1415 GMT, the national road traffic information centre said.
